pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 87 The Behavioral Biases of Individuals - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 87 The Behavioral Biases of Individuals
question_en: Steven Murphy has a tendency of overreacting to current events and trading too much based on news or anecdotes. Which of the following biases does Murphy most likely exhibit?
explanation_en: Availability bias is putting undue emphasis on information that is readily available, easy to recall, or based narrowly on personal experience or knowledge. Loss aversion arises from feeling more pain from a loss than pleasure from an equal gain. Overconfidence bias occurs when market participants overestimate their own intuitive ability.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 87 The Behavioral Biases of Individuals - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 87 The Behavioral Biases of Individuals
question_en: Which of the following are considered biases due to cognitive errors?
option_a: Loss aversion, self-control, and regret-aversion biases.
option_b: Representativeness, mental accounting, and overcondence biases.
explanation_en: Conservatism, hindsight, and framing biases are examples of cognitive errors. Loss aversion, self-control, regret-aversion, and overconfidence are all emotional biases.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: A portfolio manager uses a computer model to estimate the effect on a portfolio's value from both a 3% increase in interest rates and a 5% depreciation in the euro relative to the yen. The manager is most accurately described as engaging in:
explanation_en: Scenario analysis involves modeling the effects of changes in multiple inputs at the same time. Stress testing examines the effects of changes in a single input. Risk shifting refers to managing a risk by modifying the distribution of outcomes.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following risks is most accurately classified as a non-financial risk?
explanation_en: Model risk is an example of a non-financial risk. Other examples include operational risk, solvency risk, regulatory risk, governmental or political risk, legal risk, tail risk, and accounting risk. Financial risks include credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risk.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: An objective of the risk management process is to:
option_a: eliminate the risks faced by an organization.
option_b: identify the risks faced by an organization.
option_c: minimize the risks faced by an organization.
explanation_en: The risk management process should identify an organization's risk tolerance, identify the risks it faces, and monitor or address these risks. The goal is not to minimize or eliminate risks.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements about an organization's risk tolerance is most accurate?
option_a: An organization with low risk tolerance should take steps to reduce each of the risks it identifies.
option_b: Risk tolerance is the degree to which an organization is able to bear the various risks that may arise from outside the organization.
option_c: The financial strength of an organization is one of the factors it should consider when determining its risk tolerance.
explanation_en: Financial strength is an important factor in an organization's risk tolerance because it reflects the organization's ability to withstand losses. Even if its risk tolerance is low, an organization may choose to bear some risks that are consistent with achieving the organization's objectives. Risk tolerance includes risks that arise from within the organization as well as risks from outside.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Buying insurance is best described as a method for an organization to:
explanation_en: Buying insurance transfers a risk to the insurance company. Shifting a risk is changing the distribution of outcomes, typically with a derivatives contract. Preventing a risk refers to taking steps such as strengthening security procedures.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Features of a risk management framework least likely include:
option_b: disciplining managers who exceed their risk budgets.
option_c: establishing risk governance policies and processes.
explanation_en: Corrective actions against individuals are not specifically part of a risk management framework. Features of a risk management framework include establishing risk governance policies, determining risk tolerance, identifying and measuring risks, managing or mitigating risks, monitoring exposures to risks, performing strategic risk analysis, and communicating risk levels through the organization.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional VaR are best described as measures of:
explanation_en: VaR and Conditional VaR are measures of tail risk, the probability of or magnitude of extreme negative outcomes in the tail of a distribution.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Examples of financial risks include:
option_a: credit risk, market risk, and liquidity risk.
option_b: market risk, liquidity risk, and tax risk.
option_c: solvency risk, credit risk, and market risk.
explanation_en: Credit risk, market risk, and liquidity risk are examples of financial risk. Solvency risk and tax risk are classified as non-financial risks.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Operational risk is most accurately described as the risk that:
option_a: human error or faulty processes will cause losses.
option_b: the organization will run out of operating cash.
option_c: extreme events are more likely than managers have assumed.
explanation_en: Operational risk arises from faulty processes or human error within the organization. Solvency risk is the risk that the organization will run out of cash and therefore be unable to continue operating. Tail risk is the risk that extreme events are more likely than the organization's managers have assumed.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Measures of interest rate sensitivity least likely include:
explanation_en: Beta measures the market risk of an asset or portfolio. Duration measures the interest rate sensitivity of the value of a fixed-income security or portfolio. Rho measures the interest rate sensitivity of the value of a derivative.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Portofolio management part 2\Reading 88 Introduction to Risk Management - Answers.pdf
question_en: Risk governance is best described as:
option_b: allocating an organization’s resources by considering their risk characteristics.
option_c: senior management’s oversight of the organization’s risk management.
explanation_en: Risk governance is a general term that encompasses multiple functions of senior management. Determining the risk tolerance of the organization and allocating the organization's resources by considering their risk characteristics (risk budgeting) are elements of management's risk governance responsibility.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 1 Rates and Returns - Answers.pdf
question_en: Assume an investor makes the following investments: Today, she purchases a share of stock in Redwood Alternatives for $50.00. After one year, she purchases an additional share for $75.00. After one more year, she sells both shares for $100.00 each. There are no transaction costs or taxes. The investor's required return is 35.0%. During year one, the stock paid a $5.00 per share dividend. In year two, the stock paid a $7.50 per share dividend. The time-weighted return is:
explanation_en: To calculate the time-weighted return: Step 1: Separate the time periods into holding periods and calculate the return over that period: Holding period 1: P0 = $50.00 D1 = $5.00 P1 = $75.00 (from information on second stock purchase) HPR1  = (75 – 50 + 5) / 50 = 0.60, or 60% Holding period 2: P1 = $75.00 D2 = $7.50 P2 = $100.00 HPR2  = (100 – 75 + 7.50) / 75 = 0.433, or 43.3%. Step 2: Use the geometric mean to calculate the return over both periods Return = [(1 + HPR1) × (1 + HPR2)]1/2 – 1 = [(1.60) × (1.433)]1/2 – 1 = 0.5142, or 51.4%.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 1 Rates and Returns - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor expects a stock currently selling for $20 per share to increase to $25 by year- end. The dividend last year was $1 but he expects this year's dividend to be $1.25. What is the expected holding period return on this stock?
explanation_en: Return = [dividend + (ending value – beginning value)] / beginning price value = [1.25 + (25 – 20)] / 20 = 6.25 / 20 = 0.3125

question_en: If a stock decreases from $90 to $80, the continuously compounded rate of return for the period is:
explanation_en: This is given by the natural logarithm of the new price divided by the old price; ln(80 / 90) = -0.1178.

question_en: Wei Zhang has funds on deposit with Iron Range bank. The funds are currently earning 6% interest. If he withdraws $15,000 to purchase an automobile, the 6% interest rate can be best thought of as a(n):
explanation_en: Since Wei will be foregoing interest on the withdrawn funds, the 6% interest can be best characterized as an opportunity cost — the return he could earn by postponing his auto purchase until the future.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 1 Rates and Returns - Answers.pdf
question_en: Vega research has been conducting investor polls for Third State Bank. They have found the most investors are not willing to tie up their money in a 1-year (2-year) CD unless they receive at least 1.0% (1.5%) more than they would on an ordinary savings account. If the savings account rate is 3%, and the bank wants to raise funds with 2-year CDs, the yield must be at least:
option_a: 4.0%, and this represents a required rate of return.
option_b: 4.5%, and this represents a discount rate.
option_c: 4.5%, and this represents a required rate of return.
explanation_en: Since we are taking the view of the minimum amount required to induce investors to lend funds to the bank, this is best described as a required rate of return. Based upon the numerical information, the rate must be 4.5% (= 3.0 + 1.5).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Quantitative Method\Reading 1 Rates and Returns - Answers.pdf
question_en: Selmer Jones has just inherited some money and wants to set some of it aside for a vacation in Hawaii one year from today. His bank will pay him 5% interest on any funds he deposits. In order to determine how much of the money must be set aside and held for the trip, he should use the 5% as a:
explanation_en: He needs to figure out how much the trip will cost in one year, and use the 5% as a discount rate to convert the future cost to a present value. Thus, in this context the rate is best viewed as a discount rate.
